# Lab 20.2: Jobs Explorer

## What We Are Going to Do
Use Jobs explorer to filter jobs by user, state and cost, and find the most expensive queries.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Open Jobs explorer.** **Administration → Jobs explorer**. Location **US**, last 7 days.

2. **[Console] Filter.**
   - **State**: Failed → read the error messages
   - **Job type**: Query
   - **User**: your email
   - Sort by **Bytes billed** descending

3. **[Console] Inspect a job.** Click the top job. Open its query text, execution graph and performance insights.

4. **[SQL] Top 10 most expensive queries.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  job_id, user_email,
  ROUND(total_bytes_billed / POW(1024, 3), 2) AS gib_billed,
  ROUND(total_slot_ms / 1000 / 60, 1) AS slot_minutes,
  LEFT(REGEXP_REPLACE(query, r'\s+', ' '), 80) AS query_start
FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT
WHERE creation_time &gt; TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
  AND job_type = 'QUERY'
ORDER BY total_bytes_billed DESC
LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Filters | State, type, user, time, location |
| Top cost | Sort by bytes billed or slot time |
| Detail | Query, plan and insights per job |
| SQL | Same answers from JOBS_BY_PROJECT |
